reading: the act of looking at and understanding written words
Reading before bed has become part of her nightly routine.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
screens: flat surfaces of devices that display images or text
Most classrooms now have large touch screens instead of chalkboards.
paper: thin material made from wood pulp, used for writing or printing
He scribbled the address on a scrap of paper.
the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
difference: the way in which two things are not the same

is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
smaller: less large in size, amount, or degree, compared with something else

than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
arguments: reasons given to support an idea, or disagreements

suggest: to put forward an idea or possibility

and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses

it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
where: It changes where the effort goes, away from the comfortable hours of reading.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
people: human beings in general, considered as a group of individuals
Many people prefer walking to work during the warm summer months.
look: to direct one's eyes in order to see

for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
question: /ˈkwestʃən/
n

câu hỏi, vấn đề

query
inquiry
issue
sounds: gives a particular impression when heard or considered

simple: easy to understand or do; not complicated

do: to perform an action, or an auxiliary verb used in questions and negatives

understand: to grasp the meaning or nature of something

less: He eats less meat now than he used to.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject

read: looked at and understood written words

screen: the flat surface of a device that displays images or text

has: has; present tense of have, third person singular

been: past participle of be, used to show a completed state or experience

studied: The disease has been studied closely for several decades.
thirty: My grandmother has lived in this house for thirty years.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
honest: truthful and sincere; not lying or cheating
Please give me an honest opinion about my writing.
summary: a brief statement of the main points of something
She gave a short summary of the meeting to her manager.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
gap: a difference or space between two things
The gap between rich and poor neighbourhoods keeps growing.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
usually: A machine that appears to be held up by one principle is usually held up by several.
small: not large in size, amount, or degree
They live in a small apartment near the city center.
highly: The results are highly dependent on how the test was designed.
dependent: relying on or determined by something else
Plant growth is highly dependent on sunlight and water.
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
being: existing, or the fact of existing in a particular state
Being tired all week, she decided to cancel her weekend plans.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
short: small in length, distance, or duration
The meeting was surprisingly short this week.
article: a piece of writing published in a newspaper or magazine
She wrote an article about renewable energy for the local paper.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
often: He often walks to work instead of taking the bus.
too: The height of the band carries information too.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient

measure: to find the size, amount, or degree of something
Scientists use special instruments to measure air pollution levels.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
dense: having parts that are closely packed together
The hikers got lost in the dense forest before nightfall.
text: written words, especially the main body of a book or document

be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality

reorganised: arranged again in a new or better way
The filing system was completely reorganised last month.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
mind: a person's thoughts, opinions, or way of thinking
After weeks of doubt, she finally made up her mind to move abroad.
an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
argument: a reason or set of reasons given to support an idea
Her argument convinced most of the committee to change the policy.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
stages: points or periods in a process of development
The building work will be completed in three stages.
chapter: a main division of a book
The final chapter reveals the true identity of the killer.
must: used to show that something is necessary or certain
You must show identification before entering the building.
summarised: expressed briefly, covering the main points
The report was neatly summarised on a single page.
afterwards: The rain stopped, and the sun came out shortly afterwards.
tends: is likely to do or be something, usually
The market tends to be quieter on rainy weekday mornings.
come: to move toward or arrive at a particular place; to originate from
Most of the fruit here comes from small family farms.
out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
ahead: in a forward direction; in advance
The team stayed one point ahead until the final minute.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
explanation: a statement or account that makes something clear

physical: relating to the body or the material world rather than the mind
Regular physical activity helps maintain a healthy heart and body.
printed: produced text or images on paper using a machine
The invitations were printed on thick cream-coloured card for the wedding.
page: one side of a sheet of paper in a book or document
She turned the page slowly, savouring the final chapter.
never: at no time; not on any occasion

moves: A skilled cyclist moves the handlebars only slightly to stay balanced.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
position: the place where something is located
She adjusted the position of the lamp on her desk.
book: a written or printed work with pages bound together
She borrowed a book about ancient history from the library.
distance: the amount of space between two places or things
It's a short distance from here to the nearest train station.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
edge: the outer boundary or line where something ends
She placed the cup carefully near the edge of the table.
even: used to emphasise something surprising or extreme

thickness: the distance between the opposite surfaces of something
The engineer measured the thickness of the metal sheet.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
still: continuing to be the case; even more so
Despite the rain, the match still went ahead as planned.
right: correct or suitable for a particular situation
Choosing the right moment to speak up can be difficult.
all: the whole quantity or extent of something
She spent all summer preparing for the entrance exam.
gives: The charity gives food and shelter to homeless families.
reader: Every reader interprets a poem slightly differently.
rough: not smooth; having an uneven surface
The rough path made cycling slow and uncomfortable.
map: a drawing representing the features of an area
He unfolded a paper map to plan the day's route.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
effort: physical or mental energy used to do something
Learning a new language takes years of steady effort.
scrolling: moving continuously up or down on a screen
A scrolling news ticker ran along the bottom of the screen.
erases: removes something completely, such as writing or a memory
A scrolling page erases the map every time it moves.
every: used to refer to each member of a group without exception
Somebody must repaint the roof every few years.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
second: coming after the first in order
The second attempt succeeded where the first had failed.
nothing: There was nothing left in the fridge by Friday evening.
device: a machine or tool made for a particular purpose
This small device can measure your heart rate accurately.
concerns: relates to or is about a particular matter
This chapter concerns the history of the ancient trade routes.
readers: The newspaper lost many readers after it moved behind a paywall.
expect: to think or believe something will happen
It concerns what readers expect when they open a serious book.
are: present tense form of 'to be' used with you, we, they
They are planning to visit their grandparents next weekend.
skim: to read or look through something quickly without close attention
I only had time to skim the report before the meeting.
notifications: messages that alert someone to new information, e.g. on a phone
He turned off notifications so he could focus on studying.
headlines: titles printed at the top of newspaper articles
Most readers only skim the headlines before scrolling on.
messages: short pieces of information sent to someone
He deletes old messages from his phone every few weeks.
finished: completed or brought to an end
The house was finally finished after a year of building.
seconds: units of time, sixty of which make a minute
The whole process took only a few seconds to complete.
habit: a thing done regularly, almost without thinking
Checking his phone first thing every morning became a habit.
follows: comes after something in time or order
A short quiz follows each chapter of the textbook.
onto: to a position on the surface of something
The cat jumped onto the windowsill to watch the birds.
difficult: not easy to do or understand
Learning a new language can be difficult at first.
skimming: reading or looking through something quickly without close attention
Skimming the textbook the night before an exam rarely works well.
produces: The volcano regularly produces small clouds of ash and steam.
exactly: in a way that is precise or correct in every detail
A fact heard once looks exactly like one that will never be needed.
result: something that happens because of an action or event
The delay was a direct result of the heavy storm.
you: used to refer to the person being spoken to
The method also feels worse while you are doing it.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
predict: say that something will happen in the future
Economists tried to predict how the new tax would affect small businesses.
consistent: always behaving or happening in the same way
The runner kept a consistent pace throughout the entire race.
finding: a piece of information discovered through research
The study's main finding surprised even the researchers.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
comprehension: the ability to understand something, especially written text
The test measures reading comprehension rather than vocabulary alone.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
confidence: a feeling of being sure about one's own abilities
Winning the first match gave the team real confidence.
repeatedly: nhiều lần, lặp đi lặp lại
She repeatedly asked him to slow the car down.
judge: to form an opinion about something after careful thought
Coaches judge a player's potential by watching how they train.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
understood: past tense of understand; grasped the meaning of something
Readers on screens repeatedly judge that they have understood more than they actually have.
more: to a greater degree or extent
Careful listeners remember song lyrics more clearly than plain speech.
actually: in fact; really, contrary to what might be expected
The film was actually shot in a different country than the story suggests.
estimate: an approximate calculation or judgement of a value

closer: nearer in distance, time, or resemblance
The estimate got closer to the actual figure with each attempt.
truth: the quality of being in accordance with fact; something that is true
On paper, the estimate is closer to the truth.
danger: the possibility of harm, injury, or loss
Climbers must be aware of the danger of sudden storms in the mountains.
therefore: for that reason; as a result
The road was closed; therefore we took a different route.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
decision: a choice or judgment made after considering options
Choosing a university was the hardest decision she had made so far.
encourages: gives someone support or confidence to do something
The app encourages users to walk a little more each day.
stop: to come to an end or cause something to end
The bus will stop right outside the school gate.
early: before the usual or expected time
She always arrives early for important meetings.
none: not any of a group of people or things
None of the students had heard of the composer before.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
argues: gives reasons to support an opinion
The report argues for stricter regulation of online advertising.
abandoning: the act of stopping or giving something up completely
Abandoning the plan at the last minute caused confusion among the team.
which: used to ask about or refer to a specific choice
It is one of the clearest ways in which a city changes its weather.
both: the two of something, referring to two things together
Both students finished the exam well before the time limit.
impractical: not sensible or realistic to do
Carrying a full suitcase up the mountain was clearly impractical.
unnecessary: not needed; more than is required
Sometimes replanting is unnecessary: clear the ground, wait, and the old community returns.
treating: present participle of treat; dealing with or handling something
It argues for treating a serious text on a screen the way you would treat it on paper.
serious: requiring careful thought or attention; not casual
He gave a serious answer instead of joking as usual.
way: As a way of saving money, it is easy to copy and abandon.
treat: to deal with, handle, or behave towards someone or something in a particular way
Historians treat that story with caution.
window: an opening in a wall for light and air; a short period of time
Treat a serious text on a screen the way you'd treat it on paper: one window, no notifications.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
fixed: set and not able to be changed
Employees receive a fixed salary regardless of hours worked.
rather: She chose to walk rather than take the crowded bus.
endless: seeming to have no end; going on forever
The desert stretched out in an endless expanse of sand.
scroll: a roll of paper, or a continuously moving list of content on a screen
He prefers a fixed page to an endless scroll of updates.
something: She said something that made everyone in the room laugh.
written: expressed in the form of text rather than speech
được viết, ở dạng chữ viết
For centuries, Hebrew was written and read but rarely spoken at home.
down: toward a lower position or level
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
end: the final part or point of something
Save the best joke for the end of your speech.
studies: pieces of research carried out to examine a subject in detail
Several studies confirm the benefits of regular exercise.
comparing: examining two or more things to note similarities or differences
Comparing the two recipes shows how much sugar the newer one removes.
two: Two things mark it as worth keeping.
decisive: settling an issue clearly; showing an ability to decide quickly and firmly
mang tính quyết định, dứt khoát
The manager's decisive action prevented the problem from getting worse.
largest: This is the largest bridge ever built in the country.
material: the substance from which something is made
Engineers chose a lightweight material for the aircraft's wings.
under: in a position below something; less than
A supermarket loaf can be mixed, risen and baked in under three hours.
pressure: a feeling of stress caused by demands or difficulties
The manager felt under pressure to finish the project by Friday.
shrinks: becomes smaller in size or amount
The lake shrinks noticeably during the dry season each year.
or: used to link alternatives or possibilities
Would you like tea or coffee with your breakfast?
vanishes: The morning fog vanishes as soon as the sun rises.
straightforward: easy to understand or do; uncomplicated
Filling in the online form is fairly straightforward.
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
grew: increased in size, or became older
The small business grew rapidly over just a few years.
up: towards a higher place or position

also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
passage: a short section of a piece of writing
The teacher asked us to analyze a passage from the novel.
sat: past tense of sit; was located or positioned somewhere
nằm ở, đã ở vị trí

left: remaining after others have gone or been used

side: a position or part to the left or right, or one aspect of something

thirds: plural of third; equal parts when something is split into three

near: at a short distance from a place, time or state

thick: having a large distance between opposite surfaces; not thin
He wrapped the gift in thick brown paper.
section: a distinct part of something larger
The library's history section takes up an entire floor.
remembered: kept or brought back in the mind
The old teacher is still remembered fondly by his students.
helps: assists; third person singular of help
A short walk after lunch helps digestion considerably.
again: She read the letter again before deciding what to write back.
offers: presents something for someone to accept, or provides something

equivalent: equal in value, meaning, or effect to something else

part: a piece or portion of a whole

passes: moves through, by, or beyond something
The train passes through three small towns before reaching the coast.
through: moving in one side and out the other; by means of
Brick, asphalt and concrete absorb heat all day and release it slowly through the night.
same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.
patch: a small area or part of something that differs from its surroundings
A patch of blue sky appeared between the dark clouds.
glass: a hard, transparent material used for windows and containers
The bakery display was protected by a sheet of glass.
so: used to show the result or consequence of something
It started raining, so we decided to stay indoors.
there: in, at, or to that place; used to show that something exists

location: The company chose a central location for its new office.
attach: to fasten or join one thing to another

memory: the ability to store and recall information
His memory for names and faces has always been impressive.
put: to move something to a particular position

like: similar to, or in the same way as

debate: a formal or informal discussion in which people argue different views

turns: present tense of turn, used with he/she/it; changes direction
When the frame begins to lean to the left, the front wheel turns slightly to the left as well.
attention: notice, thought or interest given to something

technology: the practical application of scientific knowledge, especially in industry

wins: succeeds or comes first in a contest

by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something

default: an option chosen automatically unless another is specified

because: They cancelled the picnic because it started to rain.
comes: moves toward or arrives at a place; originates from

alternatives: different options that can be chosen instead

attached: fastened or joined to something else

can: used to express ability or possibility

made: The table was made entirely from reclaimed wood.
behave: to act or function in a particular way

somebody: Somebody left their umbrella in the meeting room.
decide: make a choice or judgment after considering options
The committee will decide next week whether to approve the funding.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
